s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent perianal abscesses with atypical squamous cells and a fluctuant mass
key_facts: 66-year-old man
History of perianal trauma from sitting on broken glass in childhood
Comorbidities include vascular dementia, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, atrial fibrillation, and gout
No perianal warts, sexually transmitted diseases, immune deficiency, inflammatory dermatoses, arsenic exposure, or family history of malignancy
Fluctuant left lateral perianal mass without external fistulas
Ultrasound‐guided aspiration yielded 15 cc of purulent fluid
Gram stain and cultures were negative
Cytology showed atypical squamous cells
Mass enlarged over two months
Surgical drainage yielded purulent fluid without microbial growth
External sinus tract into the mass noted on examination under anesthesia

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Atypical squamous cells found in cytology

shortlist.label: Perianal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent perianal abscesses and purulent fluid found in aspiration

shortlist.label: Fistula-in-ano
shortlist.why_kept: External sinus tract into the mass noted on examination under anesthesia

shortlist.label: Anorectal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Fluctuant left lateral perianal mass without external fistulas

shortlist.label: Condyloma acuminatum
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of atypical squamous cells, although no perianal warts reported

raw.rationale: Cytology showed atypical squamous cells, which is a strong indicator of malignancy, and the mass enlarged over time despite drainage, suggesting a neoplastic process

rejected.label: Perianal abscess
rejected.why: Although the patient had recurrent abscesses, the presence of atypical squamous cells and the mass's enlargement over time suggest a more complex process than a simple abscess

rejected.label: Fistula-in-ano
rejected.why: No fistula to the anal canal was noted on examination under anesthesia, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Anorectal cyst
rejected.why: The presence of atypical squamous cells and the mass's behavior over time are not typical of a benign cyst

rejected.label: Condyloma acuminatum
rejected.why: The patient reported no perianal warts, and the cytology results suggested a more malignant process than a condyloma
